name: Jamf
scope_notes: Covers Jamf (Jamf Pro, Jamf Platform API Gateway, Jamf Protect, Jamf School). Jamf Pro cloud (11.x) is the main focus; Jamf Log Stream export needs Jamf Cloud Premium; Protect and School covered from public docs only.

controls.name: Disable API Client
controls.what: Stops the client from issuing new access tokens; existing tokens stay valid until expiry.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > client > Disable API Client; or PUT /v1/api-integrations/{id} enabled=false

controls.name: Remove specified API integration
controls.what: Deletes the API client; already-issued tokens remain valid until expiry.

controls.name: Rotate Client Secret
controls.what: Invalidates the old secret so it can no longer mint tokens.
controls.setting: API client > Rotate Client Secret; POST /v1/api-integrations/{id}/client-credentials

controls.name: API Roles
controls.what: Client privileges are the union of assigned API roles; editing a role's privileges applies to live tokens immediately.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > API Roles; /v1/api-roles

controls.name: Access Token Lifetime
controls.what: Sets token lifetime in seconds per client; changes do not affect tokens already issued.

controls.name: Token scope parameter
controls.what: Caller may request a token limited to a subset of the client's roles.

controls.name: Invalidate current token
controls.what: Invalidates the bearer token presented in the request (self-revoke by the holder).

controls.name: Password Policy
controls.what: Sets lockout attempts, password length/age/reuse for local Jamf Pro accounts used to mint bearer tokens.
controls.setting: Settings > System > User accounts & groups > Password Policy

controls.name: Jamf Pro user account privileges
controls.what: Bearer token carries the account's privilege set; CRUD privileges map to POST/GET/PUT/DELETE.

controls.name: Integration scope level and capability permissions
controls.what: Each gateway integration is bound to one scope level (org, environment, tenant) and granted capability:action permissions.

controls.name: Integration validity (six months)
controls.what: Gateway integrations expire after six months.

controls.name: Jamf Protect API client role
controls.what: Each Protect API client is assigned a role such as Read Only; max five clients.

controls.name: Jamf School API key methods
controls.what: Each key is limited to the API methods selected for it.
controls.setting: Organization > Settings > API > Add API Key

controls.name: Access Status (Jamf Pro user account)
controls.what: An admin can set a Jamf Pro user account's Access Status to Disabled, blocking that account's username/password sign-in used to get bearer tokens.
controls.setting: Settings > System > User accounts & groups > account > Access Status

no_control.what: Disabling or deleting an API client does not end access for tokens already issued; there is no documented per-client token revocation.
No SSO/IdP enforcement for API authentication.

controls_unknown: IP allowlisting for Jamf Pro API clients or user API access (none found in public docs).
Default and maximum Access Token Lifetime for API clients (the doc example shows expires_in 599, but no default is stated).
Whether Jamf Pro admins can block a user account from using /v1/auth/token while keeping UI access.
Which identity Change Management logs for actions taken by an API client, and whether /v1/oauth/token requests appear in the Access Log.
Exact Change Management object/action names for API client create/rotate/disable.
Jamf Protect API token lifetime and revocation; Jamf School API key expiry, auth header format and revocation behavior.
Platform API Gateway: revoke/disable controls for an integration and IP restrictions.

credentials.name: Jamf Pro API client (API Roles and Clients, client credentials)

authentication.summary: An admin creates an API client with one or more API roles and generates a client secret. The client ID and secret are exchanged at POST /api/v1/oauth/token (grant_type=client_credentials) for a short-lived bearer token. Works for both the Jamf Pro API and the Classic API.

federation.details: Static client secret; no workload identity federation documented. Jamf states API authentication does not support SSO.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for API clients found in public Jamf Pro docs.

lifetime.summary: Access token lifetime set per client (Access Token Lifetime, seconds); client secret has no documented expiry

renewal.summary: Request a new token with the same client ID and secret; secret is rotated manually.

administration.summary: Settings > System > API roles and clients. Admins can disable, delete, or rotate the secret of a client and edit its roles. Managed by API at /v1/api-integrations and /v1/api-roles.

sso.details: Jamf says API authentication does not support SSO; client credentials are exchanged directly for tokens.

offboard.details: API clients are standalone service credentials, not tied to a Jamf Pro user account.

inventory.details: Settings > API Roles and Clients lists clients; GET /v1/api-integrations returns them via API.

reads.ui: Jamf Pro > Settings > System > Change management (Read operations); Jamf Cloud Premium: stream JAMFChangeManagement via Jamf Log Stream

token_format.notes: Client ID is a UUID; access token is a JWT (sample token in docs is a three-part eyJ... JWT with scope api-role:N).

log_sources.name: Change Management log
log_sources.notes: Settings > Change Management; Jamf Cloud: view in UI only, not exportable except via Jamf Log Stream (Jamf Cloud Premium). Retention set by log flushing.

log_sources.name: Access Log
log_sources.notes: Login and token requests with username, IP, entryPoint. Export via Log Stream (Premium). Flushable.

log_sources.name: RestAPIOperation webhook
log_sources.notes: Fires on authorized Classic API requests; includes authorizedUsername, objectTypeName, restAPIOperationType.

credential_id_fields.notes: Client ID of the API client.
What value appears for an API client is not documented.

anomaly_cues: New API client or newly rotated secret
Role with broad privileges added to a client
Classic API reads from unexpected sources via RestAPIOperation webhook

containment.steps: Disable or delete the client and rotate its secret; to cut live tokens immediately, remove privileges from the client's API roles (role changes apply to live tokens).
containment.notes: Disable/delete leaves valid tokens working until expiry; role edits apply immediately.

unknown: Exact Change Management event names for API client actions
Whether client-credential token requests are recorded in the Access Log

calls.log_notes: Change Management records READ operations for some objects; not confirmed for API reads.

calls.reveals: FileVault recovery data for all computers

calls.log_notes: Change Management log records Read operations (shown as [READ] entries with username). In Jamf Cloud it is viewable in the UI only; export via Log Stream needs Jamf Cloud Premium.

unknown: GET /v1/auth behavior for client-credential tokens (documented for user tokens)

credentials.name: Jamf Pro user account bearer token (username/password via /v1/auth/token)

authentication.summary: A Jamf Pro user account's username and password are sent with basic auth to POST /api/v1/auth/token to get a bearer token used on both APIs. Since 11.17.0 basic auth works only on the token endpoint.

federation.details: Jamf: "API authentication does not support the use of SSO." A local (or LDAP) password is needed, so API access does not go through the IdP. The SSO settings also offer a bypass checkbox for the web UI.

ip_restriction.boundary: Access log records source IP for token requests; no IP restriction found in public docs.

lifetime.summary: 20-minute token, renewable indefinitely via keep-alive while valid

renewal.summary: POST /v1/auth/keep-alive returns a new token and invalidates the old one; or re-authenticate with the password.

administration.summary: Governed by Jamf Pro user accounts and privileges and the Password Policy (lockout, length, age) for local accounts. Holder can self-revoke with POST /v1/auth/invalidate-token.
administration.conditions: Password Policy applies only to local accounts.

sso.details: Jamf says API authentication does not support SSO; the token is obtained with a Jamf Pro username and password.

expiry.api: POST /v1/auth/token returns "expires"; POST /v1/auth/keep-alive issues a new 20-minute token

usage.ui: Jamf Pro > Settings > System > Change management (filter by username); Access log (JSSAccess.log, username/ipAddress/entryPoint) via Jamf Log Stream on Jamf Cloud Premium or on the self-hosted server

log_sources.name: Access Log
log_sources.notes: Token requests logged with username, status, ipAddress, entryPoint=Universal API; individual Classic API calls with bearer tokens are not logged there.

log_sources.name: Change Management log
log_sources.notes: Records username, object, action for changes.

lifecycle_events.notes: Access Log status value; entryPoint Universal API for token requests.

anomaly_cues: Universal API logins from new IPs
Logins from accounts that normally use SSO via failover/bypass

containment.steps: Disable/delete the user account or change its password; holder can call POST /v1/auth/invalidate-token.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether disabling an account invalidates outstanding bearer tokens.

unknown: Effect of account disable on live tokens

calls.reveals: Account, privileges, sites for the current token

calls.log_notes: Not in Access Log for bearer tokens; RestAPIOperation webhook fires if configured.

credentials.name: Jamf Platform API Gateway integration (Jamf Account client credentials)

authentication.summary: An integration created in Jamf Account holds a client_id and client_secret, exchanged at https://{region}.api.jamfcloud.com/auth/token for a 15-minute bearer token. Reaches platform APIs and, at tenant scope, Jamf Pro (incl. Classic), Jamf Protect and Jamf Security Cloud.

lifetime.summary: Token 900 s; integration credentials valid six months

renewal.summary: No refresh token; request a new token with the same credentials; regenerate secret / recreate integration every six months.

administration.summary: Created in Jamf Account > Integrations with a scope level and capability permissions.
administration.conditions: Jamf Account Administrator role or custom role with Integrations privileges.

offboard.details: The credential belongs to a Jamf Account integration, not to a user.

expiry.ui: Jamf Account > Integrations (integration valid six months; access tokens 900 s, see expires_in)

log_sources.name: Platform Audit API (GET /v1/audit)
log_sources.notes: api-gateway source records actor, method, path; needs audit:read.

containment.steps: Delete or regenerate the integration in Jamf Account.
containment.notes: Jamf's migration guide lists no invalidate endpoint for gateway tokens; they expire after 900 s.

credentials.name: Jamf Protect API client (client ID + API client password)

authentication.summary: Created in Jamf Protect > Administrative > API Clients. The client ID and API client password are posted as JSON to the tenant's /token endpoint for an access token used against /graphql. Jamf recommends the Platform API Gateway instead.

renewal.summary: New token requested with the same client ID and password.

administration.summary: Max five API clients per tenant; each is assigned a role (e.g. Read Only); delete to remove.

offboard.details: Protect API clients are created under Administrative > API Clients and are not tied to a user.

inventory.details: Jamf Protect > Administrative > API Clients shows the tenant's API clients (max five).

usage.ui: Jamf Protect > Administrative > Audit Logs > select entries > Export Selected (CSV)

log_sources.name: Jamf Protect Audit Logs
log_sources.notes: Kept one year, CSV export; records user, operation, arguments, IPs, resource ID.

containment.steps: Delete the API client in Administrative > API Clients.

unknown: Whether API-client activity appears in Protect audit logs
GraphQL queries for bulk read are not documented on public pages fetched

authentication.summary: A static API key created under Organization > Settings > API authorizes all API calls to https://{yourURL}.jamfcloud.com/api, limited to the methods selected for the key.

renewal.summary: Key is reused on every call.

administration.summary: Organization > Settings > API: add key and choose which methods it can access.

offboard.details: API keys are created at the organization level, not tied to a user.

inventory.details: Organization > Settings > API is where API keys are created and edited.

log_sources.name: Jamf School Audit Log
log_sources.notes: Retained 15 months; Organization > Audit Log; GET <domain>/audit-logs/v1 (3 months per request).

anomaly_cues: New API key with broad methods

containment.steps: Remove the key under Organization > Settings > API.

unknown: Whether API key calls are attributed in the audit log

calls.reveals: Audit log entries (3 months per request)
